title: Characterization of the role of phosphogypsum foam in the transport of metals and radionuclides in the Southern Mediterranean Sea
summary: The first chemical study of the foam that forms when phosphogypsum is dumped in seawater. The foam is heavily loaded with radioactive pollutants and is described as the main thing that collects, carries and spreads them.

findings.headline: Foam from the waste carries most of the radioactive pollution
findings.summary: When phosphogypsum is dumped in the sea it makes foam. This foam is heavily loaded with radioactive pollutants. The authors describe it as the main thing that collects, carries and spreads them.
findings.headline_original: Foam is the main carrier of radioactive contaminants
findings.summary_original: Phosphogypsum foams are heavily loaded with radiochemical contaminants and are described as the main accumulating, transporting and dispersing agent for them.

summary_original: First chemical and mineral study of the foam that forms when phosphogypsum is dumped in seawater. The foam is heavily loaded with radioactive contaminants and is described as the main agent that accumulates, carries and spreads them.
